description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacements in files.

Usage:
- You must use your `Read` tool at least once in the conversation before editing. This tool will error if you attempt an edit without reading the file.
- When editing text from Read tool output, ensure you preserve the exact indentation (tabs/spaces) as it appears AFTER the line number prefix. The line number prefix format is: line number + tab. Everything after that is the actual file content to match. Never include any part of the line number prefix in the old_string or new_string.
- ALWAYS prefer editing existing files in the codebase. NEVER write new files unless explicitly required.
- Only use emojis if the user explicitly requests it. Avoid adding emojis to files unless asked.
- The edit will FAIL if `old_string` is not unique in the file. Either provide a larger string with more surrounding context to make it unique or use `replace_all` to change every instance of `old_string`.
- Use `replace_all` for replacing and renaming strings across the file. This parameter is useful if you want to rename a variable for instance.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem. You can access any file directly by using this tool.
Assume this tool is able to read all files on the machine. If the User provides a path to a file assume that path is valid. It is okay to read a file that does not exist; an error will be returned.

Usage:
- The file_path parameter must be an absolute path, not a relative path
- By default, it reads up to 2000 lines starting from the beginning of the file
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- This tool allows Claude Code to read images (eg PNG, JPG, etc). When reading an image file the contents are presented visually as Claude Code is a multimodal LLM.
- This tool can read PDF files (.pdf). For large PDFs (more than 10 pages), you MUST provide the pages parameter to read specific page ranges (e.g., pages: "1-5"). Reading a large PDF without the pages parameter will fail. Maximum 20 pages per request.
- This tool can read Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb files) and returns all cells with their outputs, combining code, text, and visualizations.
- This tool can only read files, not directories. To list files in a directory, use the registered shell tool.
- You will regularly be asked to read screenshots. If the user provides a path to a screenshot, ALWAYS use this tool to view the file at the path. This tool will work with all temporary file paths.
- If you read a file that exists but has empty contents you will receive a system reminder warning in place of file contents.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** Configurações's "Apagar conta" is a dead action — no confirmation dialog, no `DELETE /account` call (epic-8-context.md Story 8.5; FR-43, RNF05, LGPD).

**Approach:** Add a destructive-styled `ConfirmationDialog` (red title/confirm button, `Cancelar` outline) triggered by a new "Apagar conta" button; on confirm, `AccountSettingsCubit.deleteAccount()` calls the new `AccountSettingsRepository.deleteAccount()` (`DELETE /account`), then reuses `logout()`'s existing lock+logout+clear sequence (extracted into a shared private helper) — same post-action destination as Story 8.4 (FR-42), no new navigation code.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- `ConfirmationDialog` gains optional `confirmButtonColor` (null → `colorPrimary`, unchanged default) and `cancelLabel`/`onCancel` (both null together → no cancel button, exact current session-expiry shape preserved). `AppButton` gains optional `backgroundColor`, consulted only for `AppButtonVariant.primary` (mirrors `textColor`'s existing "only consulted for textGhost" convention), null → `colorPrimary`.
- "Apagar conta": `AppButtonVariant.textGhost` + `textColor: colorError`, the scroll column's last child after "Sair" (prototype-extract.md:116). Disabled while `isDeletingAccount`.
- Tap opens `ConfirmationDialog` (title `'Apagar sua conta?'`, message on permanent/irreversible LGPD deletion, `titleColor`/`confirmButtonColor: colorError`, `barrierColor: colorScrimHeavy`, `confirmLabel: 'Apagar tudo'`, `cancelLabel: 'Cancelar'`) — reuses the same focus-trap/single-overlay widget session-expiry already uses (epic-8-context.md).
- `onCancel` pops the dialog only, no network call. `onConfirm` pops the dialog synchronously, then calls `AccountSettingsCubit.deleteAccount()`.
- `AccountSettingsRepository.deleteAccount()`/`_Impl` → `AccountRemoteDataSource.deleteAccount()` → `ApiClient.delete('account-delete', data: {'confirmation': 'DELETE'})`, success mapped to `Right(unit)` (response body unused).
- `AccountSettingsCubit.deleteAccount()`: guard re-entry via new `isDeletingAccount` (mirrors `isLoggingOut`). `Left` → reset `isDeletingAccount`, set `deleteAccountErrorMessage: failure.message` (inline, `colorError`, below the button — same convention as the biometric toggle's `errorMessage`, announced via the existing `_announce` + `BlocListener` pattern). `Right` → run the same lock+session-logout+cache-clear sequence `logout()` already performs, extracted into a shared private `_finishSession()` called by both (closes spec-8-4-logout.md's own Design Notes directive).
- No navigation code: the existing `app_router.dart` redirect (already watching `VaultStatus`/`SessionStatus`) lands on `/vault` once `_finishSession()` relocks — identical to Story 8.4.

**Ask First:** None.

**Never:** a dedicated "account deleted" screen (none exists; same destination as logout, prototype-extract.md:41,197); an undo/grace-period flow; auto-retrying a failed `DELETE /account`; changing `app_router.dart`; changing `ConfirmationDialog`'s single-overlay guard.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Tap "Apagar conta" | `isDeletingAccount: false` | destructive dialog opens (red title + "Apagar tudo", outline "Cancelar") | N/A |
| Tap "Cancelar" | dialog open | dialog closes, no network call, screen unchanged | N/A |
| Tap "Apagar tudo" | dialog open | dialog closes immediately; `account-delete` fires; on success vault relocks -> redirect to `/vault`; tokens + both Hive caches clear | N/A |

117	+## Intent
118	+
119	+**Problem:** Configurações's "Apagar conta" is a dead action — no confirmation dialog, no `DELETE /account` call (epic-8-context.md Story 8.5; FR-43, RNF05, LGPD).
120	+
121	+**Approach:** Add a destructive-styled `ConfirmationDialog` (red title/confirm button, `Cancelar` outline) triggered by a new "Apagar conta" button; on confirm, `AccountSettingsCubit.deleteAccount()` calls the new `AccountSettingsRepository.deleteAccount()` (`DELETE /account`), then reuses `logout()`'s existing lock+logout+clear sequence (extracted into a shared private helper) — same post-action destination as Story 8.4 (FR-42), no new navigation code.
122	+
123	+## Boundaries & Constraints
124	+
125	+**Always:**
126	+- `ConfirmationDialog` gains optional `confirmButtonColor` (null → `colorPrimary`, unchanged default) and `cancelLabel`/`onCancel` (both null together → no cancel button, exact current session-expiry shape preserved). `AppButton` gains optional `backgroundColor`, consulted only for `AppButtonVariant.primary` (mirrors `textColor`'s existing "only consulted for textGhost" convention), null → `colorPrimary`.
127	+- "Apagar conta": `AppButtonVariant.textGhost` + `textColor: colorError`, the scroll column's last child after "Sair" (prototype-extract.md:116). Disabled while `isDeletingAccount`.
128	+- Tap opens `ConfirmationDialog` (title `'Apagar sua conta?'`, message on permanent/irreversible LGPD deletion, `titleColor`/`confirmButtonColor: colorError`, `barrierColor: colorScrimHeavy`, `confirmLabel: 'Apagar tudo'`, `cancelLabel: 'Cancelar'`) — reuses the same focus-trap/single-overlay widget session-expiry already uses (epic-8-context.md).
129	+- `onCancel` pops the dialog only, no network call. `onConfirm` pops the dialog synchronously, then calls `AccountSettingsCubit.deleteAccount()`.
130	+- `AccountSettingsRepository.deleteAccount()`/`_Impl` → `AccountRemoteDataSource.deleteAccount()` → `ApiClient.delete('account-delete', data: {'confirmation': 'DELETE'})`, success mapped to `Right(unit)` (response body unused).
131	+- `AccountSettingsCubit.deleteAccount()`: guard re-entry via new `isDeletingAccount` (mirrors `isLoggingOut`). `Left` → reset `isDeletingAccount`, set `deleteAccountErrorMessage: failure.message` (inline, `colorError`, below the button — same convention as the biometric toggle's `errorMessage`, announced via the existing `_announce` + `BlocListener` pattern). `Right` → run the same lock+session-logout+cache-clear sequence `logout()` already performs, extracted into a shared private `_finishSession()` called by both (closes spec-8-4-logout.md's own Design Notes directive).
132	+- No navigation code: the existing `app_router.dart` redirect (already watching `VaultStatus`/`SessionStatus`) lands on `/vault` once `_finishSession()` relocks — identical to Story 8.4.
133	+
134	+**Ask First:** None.
135	+
136	+**Never:** a dedicated "account deleted" screen (none exists; same destination as logout, prototype-extract.md:41,197); an undo/grace-period flow; auto-retrying a failed `DELETE /account`; changing `app_router.dart`; changing `ConfirmationDialog`'s single-overlay guard.

143	+| Tap "Cancelar" | dialog open | dialog closes, no network call, screen unchanged | N/A |
144	+| Tap "Apagar tudo" | dialog open | dialog closes immediately; `account-delete` fires; on success vault relocks -> redirect to `/vault`; tokens + both Hive caches clear | N/A |

+## Deferred from: code review of spec-8-4-logout (2026-11-08)
+
+- source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-8-4-logout.md`
+  summary: `SessionRepositoryImpl.logout()` swallows a `clearSession()` exception with an empty `catch (_) {}` and no logging, while the cache-clear failures a few lines away in the same logout flow (`AccountSettingsCubit.logout()`) do `debugPrint`.
+  evidence: Review finding (blind-hunter layer), reclassified from Patch to Defer after inspection. The silent catch deliberately mirrors `restoreSession()`'s own pre-existing identical silent-catch convention in this same file (its own comment cites it) — adding `debugPrint` here would deviate from that established, intentional match rather than fix a defect. A codebase-wide tension between two valid local conventions (this file's silent-catch vs. the cubit layer's debugPrint-on-failure), not a bug this diff introduced. `session_repository_impl.dart:183`.
+- source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-8-4-logout.md`
+  summary: The "Sair" button shows no loading indicator while `isLoggingOut` is true (just `onPressed: null`) — every other in-flight async action on this screen (name save, biometric toggle) shows a `CircularProgressIndicator`.
+  evidence: Review finding (blind-hunter layer), reclassified from Patch to Defer after inspection. `AppButton` is a shared primitive reused across login/signup/entries/vault with no loading-slot API; adding one here means either changing that shared widget (out of this story's scope) or a layout change that can't be visually verified (no simulator/device in this project yet). Low-impact in practice since the vault-lock-triggered redirect fires near-instantly. `account_settings_screen.dart:577`.
+- source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-8-4-logout.md`
+  summary: `EntriesRepository.clearLocalCache()`/`ChatRepository.clearLocalCache()` use `Failure.malformedResponse` for local Hive disk-clear failures — a type named for malformed network responses, not local-storage faults.
+  evidence: Review finding (acceptance-auditor + blind-hunter layers, converged). Mirrors an existing convention already used elsewhere in the codebase; fixing it means a broader `Failure`-taxonomy change outside this story's scope. `entries_repository_impl.dart:234`, `chat_repository_impl.dart:163`.
+- source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-8-4-logout.md`
+  summary: The vault locks and the router can redirect to `/vault` before the awaited `auth-logout` call and the two `clearLocalCache()` calls finish; if the OS kills the app in that window, the backend session may stay un-revoked and/or the Hive caches unflushed.
+  evidence: Review finding (blind-hunter layer). Generic mobile async-during-navigation risk, not unique to this story's design, and out of scope to mitigate here (would need background-task handling). `account_settings_cubit.dart:348-358`.
+- source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-8-4-logout.md`
+  summary: `AccountSettingsCubit.logout()` doesn't guard against `toggleBiometric`/`confirmEditingName` being in flight when "Sair" is tapped — a resolved in-flight call can `emit()` after logout, stomping state with results computed before the session ended.
+  evidence: Review finding (edge-case-hunter layer). Same root cause and risk class as this file's own "logout never resets in-memory singleton state" entry above; not fixable without the broader in-memory-reset decision already explicitly scoped out of this story's frozen Boundaries. `account_settings_cubit.dart:209-235`.
+- source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-8-4-logout.md`
+  summary: No real-DI (`sl<...>()`-resolved) e2e test exists yet for the logout orchestration end-to-end, unlike biometric-toggle/name-edit's own `account_settings_flow_e2e_test.dart` coverage.
+  evidence: Review finding (blind-hunter layer, verified against the real test files). A fakes-based router test (`pumpWithLogoutFakesAndVaultGate` in `account_settings_screen_test.dart`) already proves the lock-before-redirect ordering, so this is a coverage-depth gap, not a correctness gap. `test/features/account/account_settings_flow_e2e_test.dart`.
+
+## Deferred from: code review of spec-8-5-account-deletion (2026-11-08)
+
+- source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-8-5-account-deletion.md`
+  summary: "Sair" and "Apagar conta" each guard re-entry only against their own in-flight flag (`isLoggingOut`/`isDeletingAccount`) — tapping one while the other is still in flight can run `AccountSettingsCubit._finishSession()` twice concurrently (duplicate `auth-logout` POST, duplicate `VaultRepository.lock()`, and two concurrent `clearLocalCache()` calls per repository racing on the same `entries`/`chat` Hive boxes).
+  evidence: Review findings (blind-hunter + edge-case-hunter layers, converged on the same root cause). Same risk class as this epic's own already-deferred "`AccountSettingsCubit.logout()` doesn't guard against `toggleBiometric`/`confirmEditingName` being in flight" entry above — a broader "any session-ending or in-flight-mutating action should mutually exclude the others" design decision that both predates and now also applies across Story 8.4/8.5, not something either story's own frozen Boundaries scoped in. In practice the window is narrow (`logout()`'s synchronous `vaultRepository.lock()` fires immediately and triggers the AD-14 redirect, which unmounts the screen almost immediately), and the duplicate side effects (`auth-logout`, `.lock()`, Hive `.clear()`) are individually idempotent/harmless, so this is low-severity, not blocking. `account_settings_cubit.dart:380-477`, `account_settings_screen.dart:618-657`.
+- source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-8-5-account-deletion.md`
+  summary: `tests/test-summary.md`'s spec-8-4-logout addenda report `1276/1276` then `1279/1279` passed, but the actual full `fvm flutter test` run against the current working tree (this diff applied) reports `1304/1304` — the ledger was already stale before this story started.
+  evidence: Review finding (blind-hunter layer), confirmed by running `fvm flutter test` directly. Pre-existing staleness from spec-8-4-logout.md's own uncommitted addenda, not introduced by spec-8-5; this story's own Verification section never asked to update that ledger. `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/tests/test-summary.md`.
+- source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-8-4-logout.md`
+  summary: The `_dashboardOverflowAnnounced`-field replacement for the narrative-unavailable announce-once guard (spec-8-4's own patch, replacing the earlier buggy `listenWhen`-only comparison) has no test driving a *second* `confirmedWrites`-triggered reload while `totalCount > 30` — every existing test in `account_settings_screen_test.dart` only exercises one `ResourceLoading` -> `ResourceData` cycle, and the suite's fake write-tracker hard-codes `confirmedWrites => const Stream.empty()`, so no test can currently reach a second cycle at all.
+  evidence: Review finding (verification-gap layer), confirmed by reading every test touching this listener and the fake tracker it depends on. If this fix regressed (e.g. the field's reset/set logic were inverted), the app would resume re-announcing "narrativa indisponível" on every reload while `totalCount > 30` — the exact bug the patch was written to close — and the full suite would still report green. +## Intent
+
+**Problem:** Configurações's "Apagar conta" is a dead action — no confirmation dialog, no `DELETE /account` call (epic-8-context.md Story 8.5; FR-43, RNF05, LGPD).
+
+**Approach:** Add a destructive-styled `ConfirmationDialog` (red title/confirm button, `Cancelar` outline) triggered by a new "Apagar conta" button; on confirm, `AccountSettingsCubit.deleteAccount()` calls the new `AccountSettingsRepository.deleteAccount()` (`DELETE /account`), then reuses `logout()`'s existing lock+logout+clear sequence (extracted into a shared private helper) — same post-action destination as Story 8.4 (FR-42), no new navigation code.
+
+## Boundaries & Constraints
+
+**Always:**
+- `ConfirmationDialog` gains optional `confirmButtonColor` (null → `colorPrimary`, unchanged default) and `cancelLabel`/`onCancel` (both null together → no cancel button, exact current session-expiry shape preserved). `AppButton` gains optional `backgroundColor`, consulted only for `AppButtonVariant.primary` (mirrors `textColor`'s existing "only consulted for textGhost" convention), null → `colorPrimary`.
+- "Apagar conta": `AppButtonVariant.textGhost` + `textColor: colorError`, the scroll column's last child after "Sair" (prototype-extract.md:116). Disabled while `isDeletingAccount`.
+- Tap opens `ConfirmationDialog` (title `'Apagar sua conta?'`, message on permanent/irreversible LGPD deletion, `titleColor`/`confirmButtonColor: colorError`, `barrierColor: colorScrimHeavy`, `confirmLabel: 'Apagar tudo'`, `cancelLabel: 'Cancelar'`) — reuses the same focus-trap/single-overlay widget session-expiry already uses (epic-8-context.md).
+- `onCancel` pops the dialog only, no network call. `onConfirm` pops the dialog synchronously, then calls `AccountSettingsCubit.deleteAccount()`.
+- `AccountSettingsRepository.deleteAccount()`/`_Impl` → `AccountRemoteDataSource.deleteAccount()` → `ApiClient.delete('account-delete', data: {'confirmation': 'DELETE'})`, success mapped to `Right(unit)` (response body unused).
+- `AccountSettingsCubit.deleteAccount()`: guard re-entry via new `isDeletingAccount` (mirrors `isLoggingOut`). `Left` → reset `isDeletingAccount`, set `deleteAccountErrorMessage: failure.message` (inline, `colorError`, below the button — same convention as the biometric toggle's `errorMessage`, announced via the existing `_announce` + `BlocListener` pattern). `Right` → run the same lock+session-logout+cache-clear sequence `logout()` already performs, extracted into a shared private `_finishSession()` called by both (closes spec-8-4-logout.md's own Design Notes directive).
+- No navigation code: the existing `app_router.dart` redirect (already watching `VaultStatus`/`SessionStatus`) lands on `/vault` once `_finishSession()` relocks — identical to Story 8.4.
+
+**Ask First:** None.
+
+**Never:** a dedicated "account deleted" screen (none exists; same destination as logout, prototype-extract.md:41,197); an undo/grace-period flow; auto-retrying a failed `DELETE /account`; changing `app_router.dart`; changing `ConfirmationDialog`'s single-overlay guard.
+
+## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix
+
+| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
+|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
+| Tap "Apagar conta" | `isDeletingAccount: false` | destructive dialog opens (red title + "Apagar tudo", outline "Cancelar") | N/A |
+| Tap "Cancelar" | dialog open | dialog closes, no network call, screen unchanged | N/A |
+| Tap "Apagar tudo" | dialog open | dialog closes immediately; `account-delete` fires; on success vault relocks -> redirect to `/vault`; tokens + both Hive caches clear | N/A |
+| `account-delete` fails (offline/expired/...) | any | dialog already closed; inline red error below "Apagar conta"; vault stays unlocked, nothing cleared | `Left.message` shown (unlike logout's swallowed failure) |
+| Double-tap "Apagar conta" | `isDeletingAccount: true` | second tap no-ops (button disabled) | N/A |

  ## Finding 1 — Failed "Apagar conta" announces the error to VoiceOver twice, contradicting the spec's claimed "same convention as the biometric toggle"
  
  **Violates:** Boundaries line — `deleteAccountErrorMessage`'s doc comment and the spec's own text say it is "announced via the existing `_announce` + `BlocListener` pattern" (i.e., the same pattern as the biometric toggle's `errorMessage`).
  
  **Evidence:** In `lib/features/account/presentation/cubit/account_settings_cubit.dart`, `deleteAccount()`'s failure path does two *separate* emits:
  ```dart
  await result.match(
    (failure) async {
      emit(state.copyWith(deleteAccountErrorMessage: failure.message));   // emit #1: error set, isDeletingAccount still true
    },
    (_) => _finishSession(),
  );
  ...
  } finally {
    if (!isClosed) {
      emit(state.copyWith(isDeletingAccount: false));                     // emit #2: error still non-null, isDeletingAccount flips
    }
  }
  ```
  The screen's listener in `account_settings_screen.dart` (new `BlocConsumer` added after "Sair") has no `listenWhen`:
  ```dart
  listener: (context, state) {
    if (state.deleteAccountErrorMessage != null) {
      _announce(state.deleteAccountErrorMessage!);
    }
  },
  ```

  By contrast, the pre-existing biometric-toggle failure path (`toggleBiometric()`) sets `errorMessage` and `isSaving: false` in **one single combined emit** (`emit(state.copyWith(errorMessage: failure.message, isSaving: false))`), so its sibling listener only fires once. The name-edit error listener goes further and uses an explicit `listenWhen: (previous, current) => current.nameErrorMessage != null && current.nameErrorMessage != previous.nameErrorMessage` specifically to prevent this. `deleteAccount()`'s two-step emit sequence reproduces the double-fire the other two call sites were written to avoid, so it is not actually "the same convention" the spec claims it reuses. # Step 3: Triage

## RULES

- YOU MUST ALWAYS SPEAK OUTPUT in your Agent communication style with the config `{communication_language}`

## INSTRUCTIONS

1. **Normalize** findings from all layers into a unified list where each finding has:
   - `id` -- sequential integer
   - `source` -- the `id` of the layer that produced the finding (e.g., `blind-hunter`), or merged sources joined with `+` (e.g., `blind-hunter+edge-case-hunter`)
   - `title` -- one-line summary
   - `detail` -- full description
   - `location` -- file and line reference (if available)

2. **Deduplicate.** Deduplicate only findings with the same claim and same required action. If two or more findings meet both conditions, merge them into one:
   - Use the most specific finding as the base (prefer findings with a precise location over prose-only findings).
   - Append any unique detail, reasoning, or location references from the other finding(s) into the surviving `detail` field.
   - Set `source` to the merged sources (e.g., `blind-hunter+edge-case-hunter`).

3. Then evaluate each remaining finding independently. Do not reject a finding because a related finding was rejected.

4. **Read the code before rating.** Before assigning severity, open the source at each finding's location and read enough surrounding code to judge reachability -- call sites, guards, and validation that live outside the diff hunk. Do not rate from the diff hunk alone. Severity reflects the real consequence at a real call site, not the worst theoretical reading.

5. **Assign severity** to each finding by consequence for the artifact's main consumer (software user, document reader, etc).
   Disregard any severity assigned by a reviewing subagent. Review subagents operate under by-design information asymmetry and do not have enough context to set final severity for this workflow.
   - `low` -- none or cosmetic
   - `medium` -- tolerable
   - `high` -- intolerable

6. **Route** each finding into exactly one triage bucket:
   - **decision_needed** -- There is an ambiguous choice that requires human input. The code cannot be correctly patched without knowing the user's intent. Only possible if `{review_mode}` = `"full"`.
   - **patch** -- Code issue that is fixable without human input. The correct fix is unambiguous.
   - **defer** -- Pre-existing issue not caused by the current change. Real but not actionable now.
   - **dismiss** -- Noise, false positive, or handled elsewhere.

   If `{review_mode}` = `"no-spec"` and a finding would otherwise be `decision_needed`, reclassify it as `patch` (if the fix is unambiguous) or `defer` (if not).

7. **Drop** all `dismiss` findings. Record the dismiss count for the summary.

8. If `{failed_layers}` is non-empty, report which layers failed before announcing results. If zero findings remain after dropping dismissed AND `{failed_layers}` is non-empty, warn the user that the review may be incomplete rather than announcing a clean review.

9. If zero findings remain after triage (all rejected or none raised): state "✅ Clean review — all layers passed." (Step 3 already warned if any review layers failed via `{failed_layers}`.)

## NEXT

Read fully and follow `./step-04-present.md`

Present summary Announce what was written: > **Code review complete.** <D> `decision-needed`, <P> `patch`, <W> `defer`, <R> dismissed as noise. If `{spec_file}` is set, add: `Findings written to the review findings section in {spec_file}.` Otherwise add: `Findings are listed above. No story file was provided, so nothing was persisted.` ### 4. Resolve decision-needed findings If `decision_needed` findings exist, present each one with its detail and the options available. The user must decide — the correct fix is ambiguous without their input. Walk through each finding (or batch related ones) and get the user's call. Once resolved, each becomes a `patch`, `defer`, or is dismissed. If the user chooses to defer, ask: Quick one-line reason for deferring this item? (helps future reviews): — then append that reason to both the story file bullet and the `{deferred_work_file}` entry. **HALT** — I am waiting for your numbered choice. Reply with only the number. Do not proceed until you select an option. ### 5. Handle `patch` findings If `patch` findings exist (including any resolved from step 4), HALT. Ask the user: If `{spec_file}` is set, present all three options: > **How would you like to handle the `<P>` `patch` findings?** > 1. **Apply every patch** — fix all of them now, no per-finding confirmation. Defer and decision-needed items are not touched. > 2. **Leave as action items** — they are already in the story file > 3. **Walk through each patch** — show details for each before deciding If `{spec_file}` is **not** set, present only options 1 and 2 (omit "Leave as action items" — findings were not written to a file): > **How would you like to handle the `<P>` `patch` findings?** > 1. **Apply every patch** — fix all of them now, no per-finding confirmation. After walkthrough, re-offer the applicable options above. **HALT** — I am waiting for your numbered choice. Do not proceed until you select an option. **✅ Code review actions complete** - Decision-needed resolved: <D> - Patches handled: <P> - Deferred: <W> - Dismissed: <R> ### 6. Update story status and sync sprint tracking Skip this section if `{spec_file}` is not set. #### Determine new status based on review outcome - If all `decision-needed` and `patch` findings were resolved (fixed or dismissed) AND no unresolved `high`/`medium` findings remain: set `{new_status}` = `done`. Update the story file Status section to `done`. - If `patch` findings were left as action items, or unresolved issues remain: set `{new_status}` = `in-progress`. Update the story file Status section to `in-progress`. Save the story file. #### Sync sprint-status.yaml If `{story_key}` is not set, skip this subsection and note that sprint status was not synced because no story key was available. If `{story_key}` not found in sprint status: warn the user that the story file was updated but sprint-status sync failed. If `{sprint_status}` file does not exist, note that story status was updated in the story file only. #### Completion summary > **Review Complete!** > > **Story Status:** `{new_status}` > **Issues Fixed:** <fixed_count> > **Action Items Created:** <action_count> > **Deferred:** <W> > **Dismissed:** <R> ### 7. Next steps Present the user with follow-up options: > **What would you like to do next?** > 1. **Start the next story** — run `dev-story` to pick up the next `ready-for-dev` story > 2. **Re-run code review** — address findings and review again > 3. **Done** — end the workflow **HALT** — I am waiting for your choice. Do not proceed until the user selects an option. ## On Complete Run: `uv run {project-root}/_bmad/scripts/resolve_customization.py --skill {skill-root} --key workflow.on_complete` If the resolved `workflow.on_complete` is non-empty, follow it as the final terminal instruction before exiting.

635	- source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-8-5-account-deletion.md`
636	  summary: "Sair" and "Apagar conta" each guard re-entry only against their own in-flight flag (`isLoggingOut`/`isDeletingAccount`) — tapping one while the other is still in flight can run `AccountSettingsCubit._finishSession()` twice concurrently (duplicate `auth-logout` POST, duplicate `VaultRepository.lock()`, and two concurrent `clearLocalCache()` calls per repository racing on the same `entries`/`chat` Hive boxes).
637	  evidence: Review findings (blind-hunter + edge-case-hunter layers, converged on the same root cause). Same risk class as this epic's own already-deferred "`AccountSettingsCubit.logout()` doesn't guard against `toggleBiometric`/`confirmEditingName` being in flight" entry above — a broader "any session-ending or in-flight-mutating action should mutually exclude the others" design decision that both predates and now also applies across Story 8.4/8.5, not something either story's own frozen Boundaries scoped in. In practice the window is narrow (`logout()`'s synchronous `vaultRepository.lock()` fires immediately and triggers the AD-14 redirect, which unmounts the screen almost immediately), and the duplicate side effects (`auth-logout`, `.lock()`, Hive `.clear()`) are individually idempotent/harmless, so this is low-severity, not blocking. `account_settings_cubit.dart:380-477`, `account_settings_screen.dart:618-657`.
638	- source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-8-5-account-deletion.md`

640	  evidence: Review finding (blind-hunter layer), confirmed by running `fvm flutter test` directly. Pre-existing staleness from spec-8-4-logout.md's own uncommitted addenda, not introduced by spec-8-5; this story's own Verification section never asked to update that ledger. `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/tests/test-summary.md`.
641	- source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-8-4-logout.md`
642	  summary: The `_dashboardOverflowAnnounced`-field replacement for the narrative-unavailable announce-once guard (spec-8-4's own patch, replacing the earlier buggy `listenWhen`-only comparison) has no test driving a *second* `confirmedWrites`-triggered reload while `totalCount > 30` — every existing test in `account_settings_screen_test.dart` only exercises one `ResourceLoading` -> `ResourceData` cycle, and the suite's fake write-tracker hard-codes `confirmedWrites => const Stream.empty()`, so no test can currently reach a second cycle at all.
643	  evidence: Review finding (verification-gap layer), confirmed by reading every test touching this listener and the fake tracker it depends on. If this fix regressed (e.g. the field's reset/set logic were inverted), the app would resume re-announcing "narrativa indisponível" on every reload while `totalCount > 30` — the exact bug the patch was written to close — and the full suite would still report green. Supersedes/replaces the still-present but now-stale sibling entry above ("The `DashboardCubit` `BlocListener`'s `listenWhen` guard... has no test driving two qualifying emissions") describing the old, now-replaced mechanism. `account_settings_screen.dart:69,581-602`.

  summary: No real-DI (`sl<...>()`-resolved) e2e test exists yet for `deleteAccount()`'s orchestration end-to-end, unlike the new real-DI e2e group this same diff adds for `logout()`.
  evidence: Review finding (blind-hunter layer, 2026-11-08 code-review run), confirmed against the real test files — `account_settings_flow_e2e_test.dart` gained a "Story 8.4 — logout" real-DI group in this diff but no equivalent "Story 8.5 — account deletion" group. [lib/features/account/presentation/cubit/account_settings_cubit.dart:471-480; lib/features/account/presentation/screens/account_settings_screen.dart:627-631]

[test/features/account/presentation/screens/account_settings_screen_test.dart]

Findings written to the review findings section in `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-8-5-account-deletion.md`.

**Dismissed (9):** ConfirmationDialog's release-stripped assert (idiomatic Flutter pattern, no misusing call site), its untested branch (same reasoning), a cubit test suggestion for a code path that's behaviorally identical either way, an editorial nitpick about another finding's confidence wording, a process nitpick about spec-file section structure, the Hive-cache-clear sequencing (already justified in the spec's own frozen Design Notes), a suggested stricter `AppButton` assert (would break symmetry with the sibling `textColor` field), speculative unhandled-exception edge cases (contradicts the enforced `Either` convention), and the dashboard-announce-once test gap — an exact duplicate of an entry the diff itself already recorded.
